lines: You've never seen Antarctica like this.
A skull, grinning at Devil Island, in NASA's October twenty twenty-six photo.
No Photoshop. The eye is a rock peak in the ice.
The grin, glacier rubble. The jaw, a glacier called Devil's Bay.
So why is it so clear this year?
A warm twenty twenty-six winter left too little snow to cover it.
Warm. On the continent with Earth's coldest reading: minus eighty-nine point two.
About seventy degrees colder than your freezer.
Under four kilometres of that ice, there's a lake. Still liquid.
Earth's heat warms it from below, and the weight stops it freezing.
Beneath one glacier, the ground drops three and a half kilometres below sea level.
The deepest land on Earth. Four Burj Khalifas would fit.
And that's still not the strangest part.
Remember Vega Island? Scientists dug up a real skull there.
A bird, sixty-nine million years old, from the age of dinosaurs.
The fake skull was guarding a real one.
Ducks, apparently, keep a very scary family album.
Fake skull or real skull? Comment which is creepier.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
